plan.forAgent:
You are building the Project Planner app in apps/project-planner/.

The designer has handed off this design with Agent Zero Studio. Apply their exact intent:

## Design tokens (set these CSS variables in src/theme/tokens.css)
- --color-accent: #2563EB
- --radius-control: 6px
- --radius-card: 12px
- --space-row: 12px
- --text-title: 28px
- --radius-chip: 16px
- --header-style: accent

## Screens to build
- Projects List (id: projects-list): default, empty, loading, error states
- Project Detail (id: project-detail): default, empty, loading, error states

## What's already done
- Page title size: 28px
- New screen: Project Detail
- New screen: Projects List

## Designer's notes
- Every screen has its empty, loading and error states

## Agent Zero Studio conventions (keep every one)
- Only change files inside apps/project-planner/.
- The app is a static web page: apps/project-planner/index.html plus the CSS and JS files it links by relative path. No build step, no network requests, no ES module imports. Studio previews these files directly.
- Design tokens: declare these CSS variables in apps/project-planner/src/theme/tokens.css on :root and read every themed value from them: --color-accent, --color-on-accent, --radius-control, --radius-card, --space-row, --text-title, --radius-chip, --header-style (light or accent). Style the accent header with :root[data-studio-header="accent"], and set that attribute from --header-style in app JS.
- Screens: wrap each screen in an element with data-studio-screen="<id>" and data-studio-screen-name="<Name>". Mark a screen you drafted, and the designer has not accepted yet, with data-studio-draft.
- States: every screen has default, empty, loading and error states. Put each state's markup in an element with data-studio-when="<state>" (space separated when shared). Outside Studio, read ?state= from the URL and set it as <html data-studio-state>.
- Selectable elements: give each designable element data-studio-id (unique), data-studio-type (page, header, heading, button, button-ghost, input, row, card, chip or text), data-studio-name (plain English), data-studio-source (file and line, e.g. index.html:42), data-studio-tokens (the token names it reads, e.g. "color.accent radius.control"), and data-studio-text="<key>" where a designer may edit the text.

All the text content is in the committed.texts object in .studio/state.json. Use those exact keys in data-studio-text attributes, and render the text from that object.
